findings.text: `pull` uses `list.remove`, which raises ValueError when the value isn't in the list. `db.update(pull('tags','python'), cond)` is a bulk operation. If any matched document lacks the value, the exception aborts the whole update and none of the documents are changed. Removing a value that is absent should be a no-op, for example `if value in doc[field]: doc[field].remove(value)`. The docstring documents the raise, but the docs/usage.rst entry doesn't mention it. No test covers this case.

`push` appends the same `value` object to every matched document's list. If `value` is a mutable dict or list, the documents share one reference until they are serialized. Consider copying it, for example with `copy.deepcopy`. A missing field also raises KeyError, which aborts the whole bulk update and isn't documented or tested.

The tests only cover the happy path. They don't cover pull of an absent value, pull or push on a document without the field, or an update matching several documents where only some contain the value. These are the cases where the behaviour is most questionable.

`pull` calls `list.remove`, which raises ValueError when the value isn't in the list. `db.update(pull('tags','x'), cond)` is applied to every matching document. If one match doesn't contain 'x', the whole update aborts with an exception, and no document is updated. Removing a value that isn't there should do nothing. Guard the call (`if value in doc[field]`). The same pattern applies to the bulk usage the task describes. The docstring documents the raise, but that makes the behaviour a trap rather than a fix.

Nothing covers pull on a missing value, pull with duplicates (only the first occurrence is removed, which is undocumented in usage.rst), or an update that matches several documents where only some contain the value. The missing-value case is the one that exposes the defect above.
